utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-8/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Nenad Banovic, Predrag Banovic, Dusan Fustar, and Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good afternoon. My name is Camille Bibles. I'm appearing with Mark Vlasic for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am the Defence counsel of the accused Nenad Banovic. My name is Veselin Londrovic. I am an attorney from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Bibles, we have here the Prosecution motion to withdraw the indictment against this accused, Nenad Banovic. Since the matter is before us in open court and before we make any order, you should explain in a few words, if you would, why the Prosecutor has come to this decision and put the motion forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As the Trial Chamber is aware, this accused was charged in 1995 for actions which occurred at the Keraterm detention camp between May and August of 1992. The primary charges against this accused in that case involve the murder of three victims during that time period. Initially in this case, and until very recently, many witnesses described the Banovic twins or the Banovic brothers as being guards at Keraterm camp. More specifically with respect to these murder counts, there were witnesses who specifically describe Nenad Banovic as being a participant in these murders. However, since the accused's arrest and the arrest of his brother, in a review of the evidence, additional investigation following up on information that both the accused has provided and that we have obtained in trying to prepare for trial, leads us to the conclusion that the current state of evidence will not support a finding beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant has been involved in the significant charges of the indictment. In short, we can show that he was at Keraterm on occasion. He was not a guard at Keraterm. He may have been involved in assaultive behaviour there, but we cannot prove beyond a reasonable doubt beyond that. There are several issues that come about that lead us to that conclusion. When he and his brother were arrested, his brother, Predrag Banovic, took exceptional steps to make it clear to the arresting individuals that while it was understood that he was being sought by this Tribunal, that his brother Nenad should not be here. Nenad additionally went further at the same time to say that he did not go to the camp, that he did not work at the camp, and that he shouldn't be here. We immediately began following up on that information and ultimately the results are this motion. First, with respect to the witnesses who described or who said that Nenad was a participant in the murder of these three victims, we have established that the bulk of these witnesses are either unavailable or are no longer willing to testify. In light of Predrag's comments, the accused's brother, we went to the remaining witnesses who talk about Nenad Banovic being involved in those murders, and we pointedly asked for specific physical descriptions of the Banovic who was involved in those murders. We've also sought out witnesses who knew the Banovic twins prior to Keraterm, specifically witnesses who may have had contact or who did have contact with the Banovics during May to August of 1992, and with those witnesses, finding those witnesses, we have now individuals who can describe physical differences between Predrag Banovic and Nenad Banovic during that time period. There was a difference in the length of their hair and some other aspects of their appearance at the time. The appearance of Predrag Banovic, the accused's twin brother, matches the physical description that the witnesses give for the individuals involved in those murders. We -- and I should be up front, throughout this process, we have advised both the accused and his counsel of our concerns about this since the initial arrest. We have asked since the beginning for their assistance in the way of clarifying those physical differences that may have occurred during that time period and specifically with respect to the accused's position at Keraterm, if any. As the evidence developed and we began to see that there were problems in this case, we also approached the accused and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- provisional release while we sorted out the rest of the evidence. The accused indicated to us through his counsel that he was not interested in that, that in fact he felt that the evidence would show that he would -- that we would in fact be filing this motion and that when he left The Hague, in short, he wanted it to be for good. We did have the opportunity to interview Nenad Banovic in February. At that time, he did several things for us that were helpful with respect to this motion. First, he confirmed those physical disparities between himself and his twin brother --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Second, he also set out and explained to us that his brother, Predrag, was a camp guard. But most importantly for this motion, he presented documentation and evidence that he in fact was in Prijedor during that period but that he had assignments in other locations. And he was able to show duty rosters. He was able to show the other locations that he was at. The problem for us with the interview is that he denies ever having been at Keraterm. We can tell the Court that we do have viable evidence from witnesses who can distinguish between the two twins that Nenad was in fact at Keraterm on occasions. We have some evidence that suggests that he may have been involved in assaultive behaviour. But the issue for us has been trying to establish what we can prove beyond a reasonable doubt with respect to his participation at Keraterm, and our answer, after the vigorous work that we've put into it in the last few months, is that we do not now have sufficient evidence to convict him for offences that are the focus of this Tribunal. We're satisfied that the present motion should be granted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It seems that that's a proper course taken by the Prosecution. Mr. Londrovic, is there anything you want to say about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only wish to say that the Defence made efforts to cooperate, and I believe that the evidence we provided to the Prosecution contributed to the Prosecution reaching the conclusion it has. I have nothing else to say but to support the motion put in by the Prosecution and to ask the Chamber to withdraw the charges against my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Londrovic. The Trial Chamber has had the opportunity of considering this motion. We approve the course taken by the Prosecution. We grant the motion to withdraw the indictment against this accused. We order his immediate release from the Detention Unit, subject to practical arrangements being made with the host country. We instruct the Registrar to take all the necessary measures to render this order enforceable immediately. The Court will adjourn. I'll hand in the order.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Motion Hearing adjourned at
